source.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
source.authors: Srikanth Malla; Chi-Ho Choi; J. Choi

record.tranche_reason: Applies the benign fine-tuning attack associated with the original work—100 benign Alpaca examples, 200 training steps—and measures refusal on harmful-prompt benchmarks in additional models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports geometric measurements of safety updates, but these are not per-token KL measurements and do not test first-token concentration. It does not test compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or localization in a small set of parameters. The harmful-output classifier results are included because the paper compares them with regex scoring and they change the estimated size of the effect. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Runs Qi et al.'s benign-Alpaca fine-tuning attack (100 examples, 200 steps, lr 2e-5) on three shipped instruct models. It measures refusal before and after on AdvBench, HarmBench and StrongReject under a regex judge and a Llama-Guard-3 judge, so its own results bear on V2. The same attack is also applied to its own OLMo SFT+DPO installs and to from-scratch co-trained models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that 100 benign examples cut post-hoc AdvBench refusal by 35–38 pp on Qwen and Llama, which they explain as a thin weight-space 'suppression' install that masks rather than erases capability. Qwen ends below its own base's refusal. Continuous safety co-training during pretraining loses only 2–14 pp to the same attack, while a windowed schedule installs none. Absolute rates depend on the detector, but the authors say the orderings hold. Mistral has too little refusal to test.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the benign Alpaca fine-tuning attack, with 100 examples and 200 steps at lr=2 × 10−5. The study evaluates Qwen, Llama, and Mistral instruct models rather than the models in the original attack study.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark and refusal judge affect the measured change. Regex and classifier scores differ, and the effect also varies across models; the paper reports near-zero starting refusal for Mistral.

fits_no_version.finding: The post-hoc safety update ∆ is nearly orthogonal to the capability Fisher (ρ two to three orders below 1e-2). Its small in-subspace part concentrates on high-curvature directions, and harmful-specific hidden-state divergence is confined to a narrow band of blocks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc safety updates lie in a low-overlap, high-curvature 'suppression' regime of weight space relative to capability directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuous safety co-training across pretraining yields refusal that resists benign fine-tuning. A windowed schedule of equal total weight installs no refusal at all.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety signal that persists to the end of pretraining yields fine-tuning-robust refusal; timing alone does not.

fits_no_version.finding: OLMo-2-1B shows a sharp pretraining transition between 1B and 63B tokens, after which the instruct weights selectively engage harmful prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The representational substrate that refusal attaches to emerges in a sharp developmental transition during pretraining.

record.problems: The attack evidence is based on refusal scoring, which is not identical to harmful-output classification; the classifier changes the levels and sometimes the apparent effect size. The authors call some small changes within noise. Mistral has little baseline refusal, limiting what its results show. The study does not measure the token-position distribution or directly test the other bypass methods in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant benign-fine-tuning refusal outcomes were left out.

untested.parts: No harmful-demonstration fine-tuning. The authors say this variant is untested because it needs Qi et al.'s data.
Only one benign dataset (Alpaca) and one example count (100) on shipped models; datasets chosen to be maximally damaging are not tested.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test that pruning or isolating a small set of weights or ranks removes safety. The geometry shows a thin update but runs no causal localization.
Offers a weight-space (Fisher-kernel) explanation of fragility but does not test whether data or objective produce first-token shallowness.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first response tokens. Co-training during pretraining is a different intervention.

missing.what: Benign attack on the authors' own OLMo-2-1B SFT+DPO installs: 21.9→0% at 1B, 42.2→15.6% at 4001B, 4.7→3.1% at 105B (within noise)
Benign attack on cotrain-continuous models at 410M–6.9B, regex and classifier, on AdvBench, HarmBench and StrongReject (e.g. 98.4→84.0, 96.9→90.6 regex; classifier 91.8→64.8)
Stronger benign-SFT sweep (lr, steps) on 1B co-trained model: worst-case 75%; identity-shifting attack leaves 100%
160M pilot: cotrain-late refusal 84.4→15.6 (-68.8 pp) under the benign attack; 1B schedule runs under the classifier (82.8→65.6)
Base-model refusal context: Qwen base refuses 71.1% AdvBench, so post-attack Qwen-Instruct (58.2%) ends below its own base

record.verdict_notes: The headline effect is regex-scored. Under Llama-Guard the Qwen AdvBench drop shrinks from 34.8 to 7.8 pp, so the size of the V2 effect is judge-dependent. Mistral rows are floor-limited and should not count as absent. The paper cites Qi et al. 2025 on first-token shallowness but tests none of V3–V7 directly.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning attack is tested.
Tests benign Alpaca fine-tuning on three shipped instruct models; does not test other benign datasets or a range of example counts.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
The study tests benign fine-tuning, but not compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Does not test whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
The study proposes a weight-space account of post-hoc safety fragility, but does not test whether the data or objective produces first-token shallowness.
Tests no training method that measures whether safety is spread beyond the first response tokens.

relation.reason: The study directly measures the effects of benign fine-tuning on refusal and harmful-output classification, bearing on V2.

tranche.reason: Section 4 and Appendix A explicitly reuse Qi et al.'s benign-Alpaca fine-tuning attack and measure refusal before and after; different models and supplementary classifier scoring do not replace the replicated behavioral test.

source_check.notes: Regex detects refusal prefixes rather than harmful output; classifier refusal means an output was not labeled unsafe. Co-training's 2–14 pp erosion is regex-specific: Table 26 classifier AdvBench losses range from 10.6 to 27.0 pp; co-training comparisons lack matched initial refusal and use one run per condition.
